recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-5954; future edits to operation HTTP method obligations should be handled under the later OperationDefinition method-support issue family.
issue_request: FHIR-5954 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core OperationDefinition change request asking for an idempotent flag so clients and servers could determine whether HTTP GET invocation is allowed.
initial_application: The request was applied in SVN revision 5054, preserved in git as ed58e45af1f531ad118f3a35313f75ad16091101, which added OperationDefinition.idempotent as a 0..1 boolean to the then-authoritative OperationDefinition spreadsheet source.
additional_context: Later Published OperationDefinition issues refined the seed application: FHIR-13018 renamed idempotent to affectsState, FHIR-14960 clarified how affectsState and URL-representable parameters affect HTTP method support, and FHIR-18197 removed the misleading HTTP idempotent reference from the affectsState definition. The current fhir.ini keeps an explicit OperationDefinition.idempotent=OperationDefinition.affectsState rename mapping.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/fhir.ini lists operationdefinition as an active resource, source/operationdefinition/structuredefinition-OperationDefinition.xml defines OperationDefinition.affectsState as a 0..1 boolean with HTTP method guidance, and source/fhir.ini maps the historical idempotent element name to affectsState.

related_jiras.note: Renamed OperationDefinition.idempotent to OperationDefinition.affectsState and explains why the current name differs from the seed wording.
Clarified POST and GET operation method support in terms of affectsState and parameter URL representation.
Clarified the affectsState definition by removing the misleading HTTP idempotent reference.
